https://www.barrons.com/articles/buffett-didnt-buy-ge-stock-after-all-1526417914 Buffett Didn’t Buy GE Stock After All By Updated May 15, 2018 5:26 p.m. ET Text Size Ed Lin Updated May 15, 2018 5:26 p.m. ET
Investors who had imagined that Berkshire Hathaway Chairman and CEO Warren Buffett might buy General Electric (GE) shares in the first quarter hopefully didn't make investment moves based on that.
Berkshire Hathaway disclosed its first-quarter holdings after the market close Tuesday, and, no, it didn't own any GE shares as of the end of March. Illustration: Getty Images
Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA) did make other two major moves, however, both already known.
Buffett had announced earlier that he bought about 75 million more Apple (AAPL) shares. The actual number is 74.2 million shares, but who's counting?
Also, gone are the 2 million shares of International Business Machines (IBM) that Berkshire owned at the end of 2017.
In addition, Berkshire Hathaway bought 21.6 million more American depositary receipts of Teva Pharmaceutical Industries (TEVA) and acquired 3.8 million more shares of U.S. Bancorp (USB). Buffett's firm sold 2 million class A shares of Liberty Global (LBTYA) and sold 1.3 million shares of data-analytics firm Verisk Analytics (VRSK).
